correctness.rationale: For each nonzero 2x2 matrix the positive square-root formula follows directly from Cayley-Hamilton including singular endpoint det=0. For A=a[[x,0],[sqrt(1-x²),0]] and B=at E22 it yields explicit symmetric moduli; trace-square reduction produces an exact polynomial identity verified by a standalone stdlib checker. The factorization gives all endpoint and interior signs, and the threshold root is unique because its quadratic sign factor strictly decreases on t>=0. Exact rational witness has gap 27/85. The claim is limited to this canonical real family.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 literature gives only an unstructured full-rank Frobenius counterexample, whereas the natural minimal structured orthogonal-input-support rank-one plus positive projection family has a complete stability/instability boundary. The exact squared defect quantifies the transition and gives a sharp geometric 60-degree onset, with a genuine positive-coupling interval and reversal as coupling increases. This answers a structural question not resolved by generic non-subadditivity, without asserting the global optimal constant.
